transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-02-14
- Time: 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Sable PM), Liam O'Connor (Sable Staff Eng), Alex Ruiz (Sable ML Eng), Samir Desai (Sable Sec)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick sync on POC metrics and integration; main topics were SDK hook for function/tool binding, structured-output schema enforcement failures in staging, clarification on streaming partial JSONs, and next steps for debug artifacts and a follow-up deep dive. Agreed to share sample code, failing cases, and a KV-cache profiling run.

Topics covered:
- SDK hook patterns (init hooks, retries, schema validators)
- Function-calling vs tool-calling semantics and how Redwood maps tool invocations
- Structured output failures and JSON validation errors in streaming mode
- Observability: token-level cost and latency traces for the pilot routes
- Security/priv: VPC egress, KMS usage, data residency note for PHI

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay, thanks everyone for joining on a Friday, we'll try to keep this tight. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Priya Nair: Priya here. Liam, Alex, Samir on.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: yeah hi all.
[00:14] Daniel Ortiz: Daniel from Redwood, hi. 
[00:16] Rina Patel: Rina here.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda, 1) quick metrics review, 2) SDK + function-binding feedback, 3) structured output failures and repros, 4) next steps.

[02:05] Priya Nair: On metrics, we saw the end-to-end latency go up on Wednesday after we flipped to the structured-output streaming flag — avg p95 jumped from 520ms to 780ms for the same 64-token prompts. Not sure if that's batching or parsing overhead.
[02:25] Daniel Ortiz: yeah that matches what we saw in logs, there was an increase in partial-chunk parsing costs. Two calls to flag — are you using the SDK streaming helper or raw HTTP stream?
[02:37] Alex Ruiz: using the Node SDK streaming helper, we do incremental JSON assembly on the client. sometimes the stream emits 'null' fragments then replays the keys, so we need to handle that.
[02:50] Rina Patel: that's likely the partial-json framing behavior; the SDK helper exposes a 'fragment' callback and a 'complete' callback, but if your schema validator runs on every fragment you will pay CPU — recommended is to run lightweight shape checks per fragment and full JSON validation on complete.

[05:12] Liam O'Connor: What about function-calling? We tried to bind a tool that makes a search in our internal clinical docs. Sometimes the model returns the tool name but with slightly different casing, e.g., 'DocSearch' vs 'doc_search', which our routing rejects.
[05:30] Daniel Ortiz: we do a case-insensitive match by default in the router, but the SDK examples show exact-name mapping; we can push a patch to make the Node SDK tolerant or provide a helper normalizeToolName.
[05:45] Priya Nair: we'd prefer the helper so we don't modify our router.

[06:10] Maya Chen: Quick question on tooling: do you want tool calls to be synchronous (blocking) or fire-and-forget with a callback?
[06:18] Liam O'Connor: blocking for now, because our business-logic needs the tool output before composing final user response. But we also care about tail latency.
[06:25] Rina Patel: yes, blocking tool calls increase tail latency; options — run tool as prefetch for common queries, or use small dedicated pool in Redwood Dedicated to lower variance.

[08:03] Samir Desai: security quick: we're sending PHI in test prompts, so what are your recommendations for KMS and audit logs?
[08:12] Daniel Ortiz: for pilot we'd recommend Private deployment, but if you must use Hosted we can enable envelope encryption and KMS integration; audit logs are available via the Console — we can share the SOC2/ISO packet.

[09:45] Priya Nair: back to structured output failures. We saw 12% of requests fail schema validation in staging. Failures look like missing fields and sometimes extra trailing commas.
[10:00] Alex Ruiz: example: {"diagnosis": "asthma", "confidence": 0.92,} — trailing comma causes parser error.
[10:08] Daniel Ortiz: that looks like a streaming-finalization issue where the model emitted a trailing comma and then a closing brace; we have heuristics to sanitize trailing commas but they are not enabled by default in the SDK.
[10:20] Maya Chen: can you show one failing trace? If you paste the request id we can pull the chunks.

[11:05] Liam O'Connor: request id is r-94a3b2f. attached it in the shared notes.
[11:12] Daniel Ortiz: pulling — yep I see the 6 fragments; fragment 4 ends with an extra comma. Looks like the tokenizer chunk cut between the number and the brace. Our chunk-merge heuristic might join incorrectly.

[13:30] Rina Patel: two options here: 1) client-side assemble-then-validate (safe, adds latency) or 2) use the SDK's streaming-safe-json mode which applies a small sanitizer and re-emits a normalized complete output; to enable: set streamingSanitize = true in the SDK init. We'll add the snippet to the guide.
[13:55] Alex Ruiz: curious about accuracy impact — does the sanitizer ever change semantics?
[14:02] Rina Patel: in rare cases it coalesces tokens (e.g., removes a stray comma), it won't change field meanings. but we recommend running unit tests with your schema-specific prompt templates to catch regressions.

[16:20] Priya Nair: another pattern: when model calls a tool it sometimes returns a synthetic explanation plus the tool result, like two outputs. Our parser expects only the tool result JSON object which causes downstream failures.
[16:35] Daniel Ortiz: that's model output control — function calling protocol should be used to guarantee structured payloads. If you rely on free-text followed by JSON, you'll see variations.
[16:46] Liam O'Connor: we're on a mixed strategy now: we use function calling for official tool invocations but sometimes use open-text when model needs to propose multiple actions.
[16:58] Maya Chen: note that Redwood's router can fallback to a 'loose parse' path that attempts to extract the first JSON blob in text and validate it, but it increases CPU and latency.

[19:05] Samir Desai: any suggestions for RBAC — we need per-route keys and auditability.
[19:12] Daniel Ortiz: Console supports per-token routing and fine-grained role policies; enterprise plan includes long-retention audit logs and SAML SSO. We'll attach the security spec.

[21:30] Priya Nair: question: the SDK retry semantics — sometimes the client retries the whole streaming call and we see doubled tool invocations. Is there an idempotency mechanism?
[21:40] Rina Patel: good point. We support idempotency keys on the request envelope; default SDK helper will generate a key but you can pass your own. We recommend tooling to dedupe side-effects on your end too.

[24:10] Alex Ruiz: on batching: we enabled continuous batching for throughput, but it looks like some small prompts get coalesced increasing latency for low-QPS endpoints. Any tuning advice?
[24:22] Daniel Ortiz: yes, tweak the batch_size and max_wait_ms per route; for low-QPS you can set batch.max_wait_ms to 5ms and limit max_batch_size to 8 to favor latency. We can compute suggested settings from your traffic trace — Daniel will run a simulation.

[26:40] Liam O'Connor: small reproducible thing — when the model returns a tool name and args we get args with single quotes instead of double quotes in some language models, e.g., {'query': 'foo'}. Parser fails.
[26:55] Daniel Ortiz: probably model tokenization; our parser tries to accept single quotes in tolerant mode but again the SDK needs to enable tolerant parsing. We'll add tolerantParse = true example.

[29:05] Maya Chen: let's talk about rollout. You're currently on Hosted pilot; is the plan to move to Dedicated or Private for production?
[29:15] Priya Nair: likely Private due to PHI. timeline tentative Q3. For now pilot stays hosted but we want to validate integration patterns first.

[31:00] Priya Nair: on observability we need token-level cost and per-route p95, and traces correlated with our request ids. Is that doable?
[31:10] Daniel Ortiz: yes, Console exposes token-cost tables and you can pass a client_request_id that we surface in traces. We can also share a CSV export of sample routes.

[33:05] Liam O'Connor: about debugging, we will share two failing examples from staging. Will you accept redacted PHI?
[33:15] Samir Desai: we'll sanitize but keep structure and edge cases.

[35:00] Maya Chen: big blockers summary: 1) structured-output streaming sanitizer not enabled by default, 2) SDK tolerant parsing toggles not set, 3) some tool-name casing and quoting issues. Agreed?
[35:12] Priya Nair: agreed.

[36:30] Daniel Ortiz: immediate actions — we'll add SDK flags: streamingSanitize=true and tolerantParse=true to the sample, prepare normalizeToolName helper, and run a KV-cache profile on your workload.

[38:40] Rina Patel: also we'll add a small node snippet for idempotency keys and show how to attach client_request_id for traceability.

[40:55] Maya Chen: scheduling — propose deep dive Wed 2026-02-21 10AM PST to go through the two failing cases and run live reruns.
[41:05] Priya Nair: that works.

[41:30] Alex Ruiz: one last question, quantization — we're considering 4-bit models. Any advice for structured-output fidelity?
[41:40] Daniel Ortiz: quantization can slightly affect tokenization and probabilities; if you need strictness for JSON output we recommend evaluating with your prompt set; Redwood Optimize has a quantization-recommendation report we can run on your workload.

[43:05] Priya Nair: ok thanks. Can you drop the SDK snippet and the security packet into the shared folder?
[43:12] Maya Chen: yes. I'll upload SDK snippet + sample schema + link to security pack. Link notes: https://redwood.ai/pilot-integration-guide (internal) and https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (spoof link for call).

[45:30] Maya Chen: recap and next steps: Maya send integration guide + snippets; Daniel run KV-cache profiling and simulation for batching; Liam to upload failing examples; schedule deep dive for 2/21.
[46:00] Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
[46:05] Liam O'Connor: thanks.
[46:10] Meeting ended.
